Kondanna And 60 Others on 19 July, 2023
Author: T.Vinod Kumar

sentences.text:
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 And
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Pulla Karthik
 Writ Appeal No. 863 of 2022
Judgment:

(per Hon'ble Sri Justice T.Vinod Kumar) This Writ Appeal is directed against the order dt.08-03-2022 passed by the learned Single Judge allowing W.P.No.13483 of 2015 filed by respondent Nos.1 to 60 herein.

2. The learned Single Judge, having regard to the law laid down by a Larger Bench of this Court in LAO-cum-Revenue Divisional Officer, Chevella Division, Domalaguda, Hyderabad and others Vs.
Mekala Pandu and others1, while allowing the Writ Petition filed by respondent Nos.1 to 60 herein,
who are assignees, had held that they are entitled for payment of compensation equivalent to the full market value of the land and other benefits on par with full owners, even though the State had resumed possession of the lands assigned in their favour for a public purpose.

entities.text:
LAO-cum-Revenue Divisional Officer, Chevella Division, Domalaguda, Hyderabad and others Vs.
Mekala Pandu and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
3. By noting so, the learned Single Judge directed the official respondents to pass necessary orders for referring the matter under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1864 to the competent authority as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of the said order.
4.

The learned Single Judge further directed that on such reference being made, the competent authority (Tribunal) shall pass necessary orders duly taking into account the judgment and decree dt.19-03-2013 passed in LAOP No.35 of 2012 and batch and any other material that may be placed by respondent Nos.1 to 60 herein.

5. The learned Single Judge also observed that the Tribunal shall endeavour to complete the entire exercise as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of three months from the date of receipt of reference from the LAO.

6. Though the said order was passed by the learned Single Judge on 08-03-2022, no concrete steps The Special Collector L.A And Another vs Mondi Pouthala Kondanna And 60 Others on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55823467/
1 for complying with the above order have been taken as of today and the appellants/State did not implement the order of the learned Single Judge on the ground of pendency of the present Writ Appeal.

entities.text: Special Collector L.A And Another vs Mondi Pouthala Kondanna And 60 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Today, when the above Writ Appeal is taken up for hearing, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition fairly states that in similar circumstances, following the dicta laid down by a Larger Bench of this Court in Mekala Pandu (1 supra), a Coordinate Bench of this Court had dismissed the Appeal of the State being W.A.No.677 of 2022.

8. Learned Government Pleader would further submit that as a matter of caution, the State has preferred S.L.P. before the Honourable Supreme Court vide Special Leave to Appeal (C) No.4596 of 2023 against the judgment dt.03-01-2023 in W.A.No.677 of 2022, and that the Honourable Supreme Court dismissed the SLP while keeping the question of law relating to claim for compensation and the time limit fixed under law open to be considered in appropriate case.
9.

entities.text: Special Leave to Appeal (C) No.4596 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
Learned counsel appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 60, on the other hand, would submit that inasmuch as the decision of this Court in Mekala Pandu (1 supra) has attained finality, which has been consistently followed by a Coordinate Bench of this Court in W.A.No.677 of 2022, which in turn has placed reliance on Special Deputy Collector and Land Acquisition Officer, Ranga Reddy District Vs. Narayan Swamy2, the question of law involved is no longer res integra.
10. Having regard to the submissions made as above and also the decision of the Coordinate Benches of this Court in W.A.No.677 of 2022 as well as Narayan Swamy (2 supra), we see no reason to take a different view therefrom which have followed the decision of the Larger Bench in Mekala Pandu (1 supra).
11.

entities.text: Special Deputy Collector and Land Acquisition Officer, Ranga Reddy District Vs. Narayan Swamy2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above, the Writ Appeal is devoid of merits and it is accordingly dismissed.
No costs.

12. On a request being made by learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 to 60 for this Court to fix a time limit for compliance of the direction contained in the order of the learned Single Judge in W.P.No.13483 of 2015 for making a reference as the time limit prescribed having lapsed long back,
learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing on behalf of the appellants/State would submit that necessary endeavour will be made for making reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 to the Tribunal within a period of one week from today.
13. The above submission is taken on record.
14. Pending miscellaneous applications if any shall stand closed.
T. VINOD KUMAR, J ___________________ PULLA KARTHIK, J Date: 19.07.2023.
